title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Theorem §92 (it begins on p.132 and ends here). Let p = λn+1 be prime. Reduce the λ-th powers 1, 2^λ, 3^λ, … modulo p. Then exactly n distinct nonzero residues occur. The remaining (λ−1)n nonzero classes are the λ-th power non-residues.

Proof as Euler gives it:
- Let a be a primitive root mod p.
- Every x with 1 ≤ x ≤ p−1 satisfies x ≡ a^m for some m.
- Then x^λ ≡ a^{λm}, so the set of λ-th power residues is the geometric progression 1, a^λ, a^{2λ}, …, a^{(n−1)λ}.
- The next term a^{λn} = a^{p−1} ≡ 1, and λn is the least exponent of this form giving 1, because a has order λn.
- Hence the n terms of the progression are distinct, the residues number n, and the non-residues number λn − n = (λ−1)n.

In modern terms: the image of the homomorphism x ↦ x^λ on the cyclic group (Z/p)^* of order λn has order λn/λ = n.

Corollary 1 (§93): among 1^λ, 2^λ, …, (λn)^λ, each residue is attained by exactly λ terms; the map is λ-to-1. In particular the congruence x^λ ≡ 1 has exactly λ solutions. If r is one root, Euler says the others are r^2, r^3, …, r^{λ−1}.

Purpose: this is the general-exponent version of the counting of quadratic residues. It is used on the next page to:
- produce numbers p^λ − q^λ divisible by λn+1 while p − q is not (Coroll. 2);
- decide whether −1 is a λ-th power residue (Coroll. 3);
- treat λ = 5 and the form ff − 5gg (Scholion 1).
errors: Corollary 1 has a gap: the λ solutions of x^λ ≡ 1 are r, r^2, …, r^{λ−1} (with 1) only if r has order exactly λ, i.e. is a primitive λ-th root of unity mod p. If λ is composite and r is chosen badly, the list repeats. For example, with λ = 4 and r = −1 the list gives only ±1. The correct statement is that r = a^n, with a a primitive root, works.

Minor: the proof assumes a primitive root exists. Euler had treated this elsewhere, but his earlier proofs of the existence of primitive roots were incomplete; that is a background gap, not one on this page.

ideas.what: Number of λ-th power residues modulo a prime p = λn+1 is n, and the number of non-residues is (λ−1)n; proved via a primitive root
ideas.modern_name: Index of the subgroup of λ-th powers in a cyclic group; power residues
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E262, E449); systematised by Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §§52–60
ideas.where_published: E262 (Theoremata circa residua ex divisione potestatum relicta), and E449 itself

ideas.what: x^λ ≡ c has either 0 or λ solutions, and the λ solutions of x^λ ≡ 1 are the powers of one root
ideas.modern_name: λ-th roots of unity mod p form a cyclic subgroup of order λ (fibres of the power map)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-known result of Euler on power residues, proved by a routine primitive-root argument. It is already in the literature and credited to Euler.
transcription_corrections: The scan's second line of the proof is partly garbled ('radix pri…tiua pro diuisore primo'); the transcription 'radix primitiua pro diuiſore primo' is the correct reading.
